main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling curry in the shared kitchen without the smell affecting the others, settled as once a week, after 7 p.m., on a Tuesday or Thursday.

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling food (Turn 1) and B objected to the smell (Turn 2). B later proposed once a week (Turn 16), which fits A's after-7 arrangement. They never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (Turns 1, 3). C accepted the Tuesday/Thursday arrangement (Turns 21 onward), which fits A's after-7 agreement (Turn 7). No direct exchange.

A-D.evidence: A asked D to cook after 7 (Turn 5). D agreed (Turn 6) and A accepted (Turn 7). D later agreed to once a week (Turn 17).

B-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (Turns 2, 3). B's window idea was rebutted by C (Turn 13). Both then accepted once a week (Turns 18, 21).

B-D.evidence: D resisted (Turn 4). B proposed once a week (Turn 16), D agreed (Turn 17), and B accepted (Turn 18).

C-D.evidence: C said the day matters because of laundry (Turn 19). D said Tuesday or Thursday (Turn 20), and C said it works (Turn 21).
